prompt: GNU make $(@D) automatic variable target contains no slash
answer:
`$(@D)` is the directory part of the target name, with the trailing slash removed.

If `$@` contains no slash, `$(@D)` evaluates to `.`.

Examples:

```make
# $@ = dir/foo.o
$(@D)  # dir

# $@ = foo.o
$(@D)  # .
```

This is the documented behavior of GNU make’s `$(@D)` automatic variable.
